To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
U6 RNA is a small nuclear RNA required for splicing pre-mRNAs and the genes for U6 RNA are transcribed by both RNA polymerase II, and RNA polymerase III.
U6 RNA is coded for in mouse by only two genes, that these two genes are at least nine kilobases apart, and that the flanking sequences of these two genes are highly conserved.
the mouse U6 RNA gene is a single copy gene that is located in the middle of the mouse genome, between the 5th and 7th chromosomes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the organization and expression of genes coding for small nuclear ribonucleoprotein (snRNP) particles.
the molecular biology and biochemistry of RNA processing in eukaryotes, with particular focus on the role of small nuclear RNAs in splicing of pre-RNAs.
the organization of U-snRNA genes in the mammalian genome.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the organization of the U6 genes in the mouse is very similar to the organization of U1, U2, U4 and U5 genes in other mammals.
the mouse U6 RNA genes are located on chromosomes 2 and 16.
U6 genes are organized into a multigene family of at least two members in mouse cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the organization of mammalian U6 genes may be different from that of the U1 to U5 genes.
there are at least 2 U6 RNA genes per haploid mouse genome.
the organization of mammalian U6 RNA genes is similar to the organization of other U-snRNA genes, but the transcription of U6 RNA is different from that of U1 to U5 RNAs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
U6 RNA may be coded for by only two genes, which are transcribed by both RNA polymerases II and III, in the haploid genome of mouse cells.
the mouse U6 genes are located in the same genomic locus as the U4/U6 small nuclear ribonucleoproteins (snRNPs), and are flanked by the same repetitive elements that flank the mouse U4/U6 genes.
the U6 gene is a very important tool in the field of biology.
